title: A phoneme, in the OpenStax chapter, is one basic speech sound
summary: OpenStax describes a phoneme as a basic sound unit, contrasts ah with eh, and says languages do not share one inventory.
body: Section 7.2 of the OpenStax psychology book says people build words by combining phonemes. Each phoneme is a basic sound unit inside one language. The chapter contrasts ah with eh. It adds that the inventory is not universal: one language's set need not match another's. The paragraph stops at sound. It is a teaching definition in the first-edition web view, not a recording of an infant's mouth and not a chart of English consonants.

sources.title: Psychology, section 7.2 Language
sources.author: OpenStax
sources.note: First-edition web view at /books/psychology/, which the preface licenses CC BY 4.0. Opened 2026-11-26. No review date was printed on the section, so the source date is the access date. Paraphrase, with credit to OpenStax Psychology. Supports the definition of a phoneme as a basic sound unit and the statement that languages differ in their phoneme sets.
